newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Oct 29.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Oct 29.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Tuesday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:
** Indian Prime Minister H D Deve Gowda told foreign business leaders on Monday said that his government was committed to welcoming foreign investment and spurring growth
He reteirated his 13-party coalition government's pledge to attract $10 billion of foreign direct investment per year

** India plans to hike subsidised oil products prices by 15 percent a year until full deregulation in 2000/2001 to bring domestic prices to international levels, an official with state-owned Indian Oil Corporation said
** The prime minister says the government will soon take steps to legally empower independent regulatory authorities to help the reform process in the infrastructure sector
** The Intelligence Bureau said the post and telegraph employees' strike had damaged the communications network throughout the country because of a lack of maintenance, the Indian Express says
MARKETS:
** Indian shares posted small gains in dull trade on Monday, with market attention focussed on blue-chips
The 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange ended 13.86 points higher at 3,264.52, off the day's high of 3,314.05
The 100-share National index was up 6.33 points at 1,451.86
STOCKS TO WATCH:

** Sandoz India Ltd said on Monday it will offer its shareholders 10 shares of 10 rupees each in Hindustan Ciba-Geigy Ltd in exchange for every 17 shares they hold in Sandoz India, under a merger proposal
** State-run Gujarat Narmada Fertilisers reported a 24 percent growth in sales to 4.8 billion rupees during April-September 1996 over its year-ago period
** Caspian Securities said it started coverage of India's Gujarat Ambuja Cements with a buy rating at 277 rupees a share. The firm set a 12-month price target of 360
The securities firm also rated coverage of India's Associated Cement Cos with a sell rating at a price of 1,545 rupees. Caspian set a 12-month price target of 1,775
** The 23 billion rupees BPL group has been restructured into six business groups, the Economic Times reports
While T P G Nambiar will continue to be the group chairman, operational responsibilities have been equally divided between his son Ajit Nambiar and son-in-law Rajeev Chandrasekhar, the paper says
** Pharmaceutical major, Ranbaxy Laboratories plans to invest $28 million in its Dutch subsidiary, Ranbaxy (Netherlands) BV, the Financial Express reports
